sections.h2: Where is the St. Francois County Recorder of Deeds and what does it record?
sections.html:
The office is on the first floor of the courthouse annex at 1 West Liberty Street, Suite 100, in Farmington, and the county says the entrance off the rear main parking lot is easier to reach. Jay Graf is the Recorder. The office records, keeps and archives deeds, liens, marriage licenses, surveys, plats and military discharge papers (Recorder page).

  • Phone: 573-756-2323, or 573-431-6505 then option 1 and 7.
  • Hours: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • Payment: debit and credit cards are accepted with a minimum $2.00 convenience fee on every transaction.
  • Search: every deed index book and every recorded document is online through Tapestry under the Land Records Search tab. A Laredo subscription is available by contacting the office.

Federal and state tax liens and their releases are recorded in this office too, and copies can be requested in writing or in person. The county Assessor (Suite 200) and Collector (Suite 201) work in the same annex, so one trip can cover a lien check, a parcel record and a tax payoff before a sale.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in St. Francois County?
sections.html:
The legislature sets recording fees under RSMo 59.310, and the county's fee page says a flat $2.00 increase from Senate Bill 938 took effect statewide on August 28, 2026 for documents, marriage licenses and plats or surveys. Ask the office for the all-in figure for your page count before you go.

Recorder fees listed in RSMo 59.310 and on the St. Francois County fee page
ServiceFee
Recording a deed or instrument$5 first page, $3 each additional page (statute, before the $2 increase)
Document that does not meet format rules$25 added to the normal fees
Release or assignment of more than one item$5 per item beyond the first
Copy of a recorded instrumentUp to $2 first page, $1 each additional (statute maximum)
Certificate and seal outside a recording$1
Copy of a federal or state tax lien or release$1.00 per page (county page)

The statute shows the 2022 text, so treat the county page as the current schedule. Whether any transfer-related charge applies to your deed is a question for the Recorder at 573-756-2323.

sections.h2: How must a deed be formatted so the Recorder accepts it?
sections.html:
The office may refuse a paper that fails the format rules in RSMo 59.310, and a document that is accepted anyway costs $25 extra. A rejected document comes back with the reason it could not be recorded. A legal description of the property is required on every document, including certified copies from a court.

  • Paper: 8 1/2 by 11 inches, white or light colored, 20 pound weight, printed on one side, no staples or attachments except where a statute requires them.
  • Margins: 3 inches of blank space across the top of page one for the Recorder's stamp, and at least 3/4 inch on the other margins.
  • Type: at least eight point, in black or dark ink, with a clear reproduction.
  • Signatures: black or dark ink, with the name typed, printed or stamped beneath each one.

Below the three-inch margin on page one, the county's list calls for the document title, its date, every grantor (using the word Grantor, plus marital status), every grantee (using the word Grantee), statutory addresses, the legal description and any book and page references. A cover sheet can carry this information. Papers signed before January 1, 2002, military separation papers, documents signed outside the United States and court judgments are exempt from the format rules.

sections.h2: Can a mistake in a recorded deed be fixed?
sections.html:
Yes, by presenting the document again, but the second filing is held to the same rules as a new one. The county requires the margins, legibility and first page information to be correct, a new cover sheet that explains why the document is being re-recorded, and a re-acknowledgment from the notary.

That detail matters when a sale is close to closing. A wrong legal description or a missing grantor name can delay the title company, so have the escrow officer review the deed before anyone signs. The Recorder also offers a free Property Fraud Alert, a notification service meant to warn owners when someone records a fraudulent document that makes it look as if the filer owns your home. You can subscribe online or call the alert line at 800-728-3858.

sections.h2: What is St. Francois County like for a seller?
sections.html:
St. Francois County lies in Missouri's Lead Belt, about 455 square miles in size, and was organized on December 19, 1821. Farmington is the seat and the largest city. The other cities are Bismarck, Bonne Terre, Desloge, Iron Mountain Lake, Leadington, Leadwood and Park Hills (Wikipedia). Public schools are run by the Bismarck R-V, Farmington R-VII, North St. Francois County R-1, St. Francois County Central R-III and West St. Francois County R-IV districts, and Mineral Area College is a two-year college in Park Hills.

The Census QuickFacts table counts 67,809 residents in July 2025 and 29,596 housing units. The county held 66,922 people at the 2020 census, up from 65,359 in 2010, and the 2025 estimate is a further 1.3% higher. Owners occupy 68.2% of homes, the median owned home was $169,300 in 2020 to 2024, median gross rent was $794 and median household income was $57,477. The county Assessor reports more than 41,075 parcels of real estate and a certified assessed value over $994 million as of 2024.

sections.h2: Who collects the tax and runs the tax sale in St. Francois County?
sections.html:
Collector Angie K. Usery's office, Suite 201 of the annex (573-756-2645), collects current and delinquent taxes and holds the county tax sale on the fourth Monday in August. The 2026 sale was August 24. Unpaid statements owed after June 30 had to be paid in full, with partial payments refused, and the office took cash, money orders and cashier's checks until 4:00 p.m. on August 21 (tax sale page).

The Assessor, Eric Dugal, is in Suite 200 at 573-756-1878. The 2026 bills can be paid at the Collector's office and online. The collector's page also lists an installment plan run with EquaPay for owners whose taxes are not paid through a mortgage escrow, and a senior tax credit. The credit was adopted by the County Commission in December 2024 as Ordinance 2024-12-10-1. Enrollment for the next round opens March 1, 2027 and closes May 31, 2027, in person at the Collector's office from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. with photo ID, and it applies to residents who were 62 by January 1 of the base year and are not delinquent. The collector's FAQ says the last day to pay without late charges is December 31 each year.

faqs.q: How do I look up a recorded deed in St. Francois County?
faqs.a: Use the Land Records Search tab on the Recorder's page, which opens Tapestry and shows the deed index books and recorded documents. You can also call 573-756-2323 or visit the annex in Farmington.

faqs.q: What are the Recorder's hours in St. Francois County?
faqs.a: The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The county website also keeps an office closures page for holiday schedules.

faqs.q: Why did the Recorder reject my deed in St. Francois County?
faqs.a: The usual causes are a missing legal description, a first page without the three-inch top margin, text smaller than eight point or missing grantor and grantee labels. The office must return a rejected document with the reason.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed with a credit card in St. Francois County?
faqs.a: Yes. The office takes debit and credit cards and charges a minimum $2.00 convenience fee on every transaction.

faqs.q: Does the Recorder collect my property tax in St. Francois County?
faqs.a: No. The Collector, Angie K. Usery, bills and collects property tax at Suite 201 of the same annex building. The Recorder handles deeds, liens and plats.
